units.sourceHTML: 3.6 Commands for sed gurus

units.text: In most cases, use of these commands indicates that you are probably better off programming in something like ⟦0⟧ or Perl. But occasionally one is committed to sticking with ⟦1⟧, and these commands can enable one to write quite convoluted scripts.
units.sourceHTML: In most cases, use of these commands indicates that you are probably better off programming in something like awk or Perl. But occasionally one is committed to sticking with sed, and these commands can enable one to write quite convoluted scripts.

units.text: Specify the location of ⟦0⟧ for branch commands. In all other respects, a no-op.
units.sourceHTML: Specify the location of label for branch commands. In all other respects, a no-op.

units.text: Unconditionally branch to ⟦0⟧. The ⟦1⟧ may be omitted, in which case the next cycle is started.
units.sourceHTML: Unconditionally branch to label. The label may be omitted, in which case the next cycle is started.

units.text: Branch to ⟦0⟧ only if there has been a successful ⟦1⟧ubstitution since the last input line was read or conditional branch was taken. The ⟦2⟧ may be omitted, in which case the next cycle is started.
units.sourceHTML: Branch to label only if there has been a successful substitution since the last input line was read or conditional branch was taken. The label may be omitted, in which case the next cycle is started.
